desc:
You are given a string s and a list pairs of index pairs [a, b] (0-indexed). For every listed pair you may swap the letters at positions a and b, any number of times, in any order, and pairs can be reused.

Count how many different strings can be obtained (the original string counts as one, and two different swap sequences that give the same string count once). Because the count can be huge, return it modulo 1,000,000,007.

s = "abc",  pairs = [[0,1],[1,2]]        -> 6   (all arrangements of a, b, c)
s = "abab", pairs = [[0,1],[2,3]]        -> 4   (ab/ba for the first two letters, ab/ba for the last two)
s = "aab",  pairs = [[0,1]]              -> 1   (swapping two equal letters changes nothing)
s = "aabb", pairs = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3]]  -> 6
constraints: pairs[i] = [a, b] with 0 ≤ a, b < s.length
s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Letters can only move inside groups of positions linked by chains of swaps. Different groups never influence each other.
Inside one group every arrangement of its letters is reachable. How many distinct arrangements does a multiset of letters have?

Find the groups with union-find. For a group of size k whose letters occur c<sub>1</sub>, c<sub>2</sub>, ... times, there are k! / (c<sub>1</sub>! c<sub>2</sub>! ...) arrangements. Multiply over all groups, modulo 1,000,000,007.
editorial: Positions connected through swap pairs form a group, and inside a group any permutation can be realised (a chain of adjacent swaps can move a letter anywhere along the chain). So the reachable strings are exactly all the ways to rearrange the letters inside each group independently, and the total is the product of the group counts.

A group of size k containing letter counts c<sub>i</sub> has the multinomial number k! / ∏ c<sub>i</sub>! of distinct arrangements, since equal letters are indistinguishable. Precompute factorials up to n modulo p, and obtain the inverse factorials with one modular exponentiation (Fermat) followed by a downward pass. Time O((n + m) α(n) + n), space O(n).
